title: Warning: you will get the songs stuck in your head. Earworms for days...
transcript: Come with me to see Here Lies Love on Broadway is from the dance floor. There are 4 different ways to view this show. 5 of you count the VIP room. And between taking a tour of the theater while it was under construction and then returning on Thursday to help film the B roll, I've kind of gotten a preview of all of the seating locations, and I knew that I really wanted to experience it from the dance floor. I love immersive theater, and I really wanted to be immersed in show. And y'all, the dance floor did not disappoint. There are a couple rules for the dance floor. One is that you can't have any bags, so there's complimentary bag and coat check. You get this cool little slap bracelet to keep track of your belongings. This also means that you can't bring drinks on the dance floor. They even give you your playbill at the end of the show. There are also a lot of moving platforms in this show. So there are that will direct you where to go, and you must follow their instructions. This is for everyone's safety. But as an added bonus, it also helps to spread around the crown and to allow you to view the show from different Vantage points throughout the show. I ended up doing an entire three sixty of the dancefloor. If you are short and there's a lot of tall people in front of you, there Are going to be moments that you miss. But honestly, because you can move around so much and you can get up right next to the platforms, and the action is literally happening everywhere, it's really not that bad. Like, truly, they are up on every single level of that theater. Now, you do need to stand the entire show. There's no places to sit on the dance floor. Honestly, it goes by so fast. The show is only 90 minutes, and because you're moving and dancing consistently, you don't really get tired. But if you do wanna sit the entire show and still be close to the action, the floorside seats are fantastic. And honestly, the view from the mezzanine is really good too. And there's a lot of action that takes place in the mezzanine. Truly, there's no bad seed in this house. Now, because there's so much happening on the dancefloor, it is such a unique experience. But if you really wanna take in the story and the entire show, I would almost recommend sitting down for your first time and then doing the dancefloor on a second viewing. But that is if seeing the show more than once is an option for you. If you are only seeing it once and you want the most immersive experience possible, I cannot recommend the dancefloor enough.
